Rashi on Shabbat 128a:11:2.hebrew: אסור לטלטלן - ואפילו הזמינם למאכל בהמה, דטירחא היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 128a:11:2.english: It is prohibited to move them - And even if one designated them for animal food, for it is [excessive] exertion.

Rashi on Shabbat 128a:12:1.english: Savory, hyssop, and thyme - Later [the Gemara] explains it.

Rashi on Shabbat 128a:12:2.english: [If] he brought them in for firewood - to dry them.

Rashi on Shabbat 128a:13:1.hebrew: שלא יקטום בכלי - כדרך חול, כדאמרן (לעיל שבת דף עד:): האי מאן דפרים סילקא דמי לטוחן. במילתיה דרבי יהודה גרסינן: מולל ואוכל ובלבד שלא ימלול בכלי הרבה, וחכמי' אומרים: מולל בראשי אצבעותיו, ובלבד שלא ימלול בידו הרבה כדרך חול. כך מצאתי בתוספתא, דרבנן מחמרי, דבכולי ידא אסור, אלא בראשי אצבעותיו. ומהו מולל? כגון אם בא לאכול הזרע, מולל השרביטין שהזרע בתוכם:
Rashi on Shabbat 128a:13:1.english: That he not pick [them] with a vessel - In the manner of a weekday, as we said (above, Shabbat 74b): "One who chops beets resembles one who grinds." In the statement of Rabbi Yehuda we read the text: "One may crush and eat, as long as he does not crush a lot with a vessel; and the Sages say: One may crush with the ends of his fingers, as long as he does not crush a lot with his hand in the manner of a weekday." Thus I found in the Tosefta, that the Rabbis are stringent, for [crushing] with the entire hand is forbidden, [and one may crush] only with the ends of his fingers. And what is "crushing"? For example, if he comes to eat the seed, he crushes the pods within which the seed is [contained].

Rashi on Shabbat 128a:14:1.english: And likewise with amita - Further on, [the Gemara] explains what amita is.

Rashi on Shabbat 128a:14:4.hebrew: צתרי - שדריא"ה לוי"ה, ל"א פוליאול:
Rashi on Shabbat 128a:14:4.english: Tzitri - Sadreie [savory; loyah, apparently a corruption of la'az, "in Old French"]; another version: poliol [pennyroyal].

Rashi on Shabbat 128a:15:1.hebrew: חשי - שדריא"ה, וללשון הראשון לא פורש:
Rashi on Shabbat 128a:15:1.english: Chashei - Sadreie [savory], and according to the first version, it was not explained.

Rashi on Shabbat 128a:16:1.hebrew: בשר תפל - שאינו מלוח, ומאן דגריס תפוח, היא היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 128a:16:1.english: Unsalted meat - [Meat] that is not salted; and [as for] one who reads tafuach, it is the same [thing].

Rashi on Shabbat 128a:16:2.english: It is permitted to move it - For he does not hold of muktzeh with regard to moving.

Rashi on Shabbat 128a:18:1.hebrew: במוקצה לאכילה סבר לה כר' יהודה - כלומר, באיסור מוקצה לענין אכילה סבר לה כרבי יהודה דאסר לאוכלו, ובאיסור מוקצה לטלטול סבר לה כרבי שמעון:
Rashi on Shabbat 128a:18:1.english: With regard to [an item] set aside from eating, he holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - That is to say, regarding the prohibition of muktzeh with respect to eating, he holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who forbids eating it, and regarding the prohibition of muktzeh with respect to moving, he holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon.

Rashi on Shabbat 128a:19:2.english: From the sun to the shade - So that it would not spoil.

Rashi on Shabbat 128a:19:3.hebrew: ואמר להו רב חסדא חסרון כיס חזינא הכא - שאתם מניחים אותה בשמש ומתחמם, וסלקוהו על פיו מחמה לצל:
Rashi on Shabbat 128a:19:3.english: And Rav Chisda said to them: “We see a monetary loss here” - That you are leaving it in the sun and it is getting warm, and they removed it at his word from the sun to the shade.

Rashi on Shabbat 128a:19:4.english: As raw meat - When it is raw, they eat it without salt.

Rashi on Shabbat 128a:1:1.english: Whose terumah was not taken - [The Gemara] initially assumed that its terumat ma'aser [tithe of the tithe] was not taken.

Rashi on Shabbat 128a:20:1.hebrew: דג תפל אסור לטלטלו - דאינו ראוי לכלום, ולכלבים לאו דעתיה למישדייה, אבל מליח נאכל חי על ידי מלחו:
Rashi on Shabbat 128a:20:1.english: Unsalted fish, it is prohibited to move it - For it is not fit for anything, and he does not intend to throw it to the dogs; whereas salted [fish] is eaten raw on account of its salt.

Rashi on Shabbat 128a:3:1.english: Asimon - [A coin] upon which there is no image.

Rashi on Shabbat 128a:4:1.hebrew: חצב - עשב שמשתרש בעומק כנגדו, ואין שרשיו מתפשטין, ובו תיחם יהושע את הארץ לישראל:
Rashi on Shabbat 128a:4:1.english: Squill - A plant that takes root straight down, and its roots do not spread out, and with it Joshua demarcated the Land for Israel.

Rashi on Shabbat 128a:5:1.english: One may move [them] - [For] it is fit for one to have elephants and feed them.

Rashi on Shabbat 128a:9:1.hebrew: על מכותיהן - בשבת, ולא גזר משום שחיקת סממנין:
Rashi on Shabbat 128a:9:1.english: On their wounds - On Shabbat, and [the Tanna] did not decree [a prohibition] on account of grinding spices.

Rashi on Shabbat 128a:9:2.hebrew: שכן דרכן לסוך - בלא מכה, הלכך לאו מוכחא מילתא דלרפואה:
Rashi on Shabbat 128a:9:2.english: As it is their way to smear - [even] without a wound; therefore, it is not evident that [it is] for healing.

Tosafot on Shabbat 128a:12:1.hebrew: הכניסן לעצים אין מסתפק - איכא למימר דה"ק: הא סתמא נעשה כמי שהכניסן למאכל בהמה, כי היכי דלא תקשה רישא לסיפא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 128a:12:1.english: "If one brought them in for firewood, he may not supply himself [from them]" - One can say that this is what [the baraita] means: thus, [if brought in] without specification, it is treated as if one brought them in for animal food, so that the first clause will not contradict the latter clause.

Tosafot on Shabbat 128a:19:1.hebrew: דחזי לאומצא - מכאן ראיה דדם האברים שלא פירש מותר, דקאמר דחזי לאומצא, אע"ג דלא מליח:
Tosafot on Shabbat 128a:19:1.english: "As it is fit [to be eaten as] raw meat" - From here [there is] a proof that the blood of the limbs that has not separated is permitted, since [the Gemara] says "as it is fit [to be eaten as] raw meat," even though it is not salted.

Tosafot on Shabbat 128a:1:1.hebrew: אבל לא את הטבל - והא דאמר רבה בפרק כירה (לעיל שבת דף מג.): "טבל מוכן הוא אצל שבת, שאם עבר ותיקנו מתוקן" — ה"מ לענין ביטול כלי מהיכנו, שלא החמירו כמו לענין טלטול בידים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 128a:1:1.english: "However, [one may] not [move] untithed produce" - And [regarding] that which Rabbah said in the chapter [entitled] Kirah (above, Shabbat 43a): "Untithed produce is [considered] prepared with respect to Shabbat, for if one transgressed and tithed it, it is tithed" — that applies [only] with respect to nullifying a vessel from its readiness [for use], for they were not as stringent [there] as with respect to moving [it] directly by hand.

Tosafot on Shabbat 128a:20:1.hebrew: דג תפל אסור לטלטלו - תימה: מדשרי בשר תפל, אלמא כר"ש אתיא; אם כן, דג תפל נמי לישרי כמו בשר תפל! וי"ל, דדג תפל אינו ראוי לכלבים. אי נמי: כר' יהודה אתיא, ודג תפל — אע"פ שראוי לכלבים — אסור לטלטלו, דכל מידי דחזי לאינש לא מקצה לכלבים. בשר תפל מותר לטלטלו לרבי יהודה מפני שהוא מאכל לחיה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 128a:20:1.english: "Unsalted fish, it is prohibited to move it" - This is astonishing: since [the baraita] permits unsalted meat, evidently it follows Rabbi Shimon; if so, unsalted fish should also be permitted, just like unsalted meat! One can answer that unsalted fish is not fit for dogs. Alternatively, [the baraita] follows Rabbi Yehuda, and unsalted fish — even though it is fit for dogs — is prohibited to move, because anything fit for a person is not set aside for dogs. [By contrast,] unsalted meat is permitted to move according to Rabbi Yehuda because it is food for a wild animal.

Tosafot on Shabbat 128a:21:1.hebrew: מטלטלין את העצמות - לר' יהודה דאית לי' מוקצה, מיירי כגון שלא הי' עליה' בשר מאתמול:
Tosafot on Shabbat 128a:21:1.english: One may move bones - According to Rabbi Yehudah, who holds [the law of] muktzeh, [this baraita] is speaking of a case where there was no meat on them from yesterday.

Tosafot on Shabbat 128a:3:1.hebrew: שפדאו אגב אסימון - הא דנקט אסימון, היינו דלא כרבי דוסא דפרק הזהב (ב"מ דף מז:); והוה מצי למימר מעות הניתנות סימן לבית המרחץ לד"ה, אלא משום דאם כן מאי קמ"ל? אבל השתא קמ"ל כרבנן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 128a:3:1.english: That he redeemed it with an asimon [unminted coin] - The reason [the Gemara] specified asimon is [to teach a ruling] not like Rabbi Dosa of chapter HaZahav (Bava Metzia 47b); for [the Gemara] could have said "coins given as a token for the bathhouse" [which are invalid] according to all opinions, [and it did not] only because if so, what would it be teaching us? Whereas now, it teaches us [that the halakha is] like the Rabbis.

Tosafot on Shabbat 128a:3:2.hebrew: ונתן הכסף וקם לו - אין הפסוק כן, אלא "ויסף חמישית כסף ערכך עליו וקם לו" (ויקרא כ״ז:ט״ו); ודרך הש"ס לקצר ולומר בלשון אחר קצר, כי ההיא דפרק הדר (עירובין דף סה.): "רבי חנינא ביומא דרתח לא מצלי, שנאמר: בצר אל יורה", ובפרק הרואה (ברכות דף נה:): "שנאמר: כל החלומות הולכים אחר הפה". וקשה לר"י: נימא כסף דוקא! וכ"ת דשוה כסף ככסף — חדא, דגבי נזקין מצרכינן קרא "ישיב" לרבות שוה כסף; ועוד, דאם כן אפילו קרקע נמי, ומנלן למעוטי קרקע? ואומר ר"י, דמכלל ופרט נפקא, כדתנן בבכורות בפרק יש בכור לנחלה (דף נא.): "אין פודין לא בעבדים, ולא בקרקעות, ולא בהקדשות"; ומפרש בגמרא, דבעי למימר: ולא הקדשות בכל אלו. לענין פדיון בכור דרשינן התם כלל ופרט: "ופדויו מבן חדש" — כלל, "כסף" — פרט, "תפדה" — חזר וכלל; מה הפרט מפורש דבר המיטלטל, כו'. ה"נ איכא למימר בפדיון הקדשות: "ונתן" — כלל, "כסף" — פרט, "וקם לו" — חזר וכלל, כו'. מיהו בת"כ דריש ליה מקרא אחרינא: "וכל ערכך יהיה בשקל הקדש" — מה ת"ל? לפי שנאמר "תפדה", יכול בעבדים ושטרות וקרקעו'? ת"ל "בשקל הקדש". אין לי אלא סלעים, מניין לרבות כל דבר המיטלטל? ת"ל "ופדה בערכך". א"כ, למה נאמר "בשקל"? פרט לעבדים ושטרות וקרקעות. אלא כן דרך הש"ס, שאינו מביא עיקר הדרשה, כמו שרגיל להביא (כתובות דף מו:): "בנעוריה בית אביה — כל שבח נעורים לאביה", אע"ג דההוא בהפרת נדרים הוא דכתיב; וכן הרבה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 128a:3:2.english: "And he shall give the money and it shall be assured to him" - The verse is not [worded] thus; rather, [it states]: "And he shall add a fifth of the money of your valuation upon it, and it shall be assured to him" (Leviticus 27:15); and it is the manner of the Talmud to abridge and state [a verse] in another, abridged phrasing, like that [passage] in the chapter [entitled] Hadar (Eruvin 65a): "Rabbi Chanina, on a day when he was angry, would not pray, as it is stated: 'In distress [ba-tzar] one shall not teach [yoreh],'" and in the chapter [entitled] HaRo'eh (Berakhot 55b): "As it is stated: 'All dreams follow the mouth.'" And [the following] is difficult for the Ri: Let us say [that "money" means] literally money! And if you will say that money's worth is like money — first, regarding damages, we require a verse, "he shall return," to include money's worth; and furthermore, if so, even land as well [would be included], so from where do we [derive] to exclude land? And the Ri says that it is derived from a generalization and specification, as we learned in a Mishnah in Bekhorot, in the chapter [entitled] Yesh Bekhor LeNachalah (51a): "We may not redeem [a firstborn son] with slaves, nor with land, nor with consecrated items"; and [the Gemara] explains in the Gemara [there] that it means to say: nor [may one redeem] consecrated items with any of these. With regard to the redemption of a firstborn, we expound there a generalization and specification: "And its redemption from one month old" — [this is] a generalization; "money" — [this is] a specification; "you shall redeem" — it generalized again; just as the specification is explicitly something that is movable, etc. So too, one can say regarding the redemption of consecrated items: "And he shall give" — [this is] a generalization; "the money" — [this is] a specification; "and it shall be assured to him" — it generalized again, etc. However, in Torat Kohanim, it expounds it from another verse: "'And all your valuation shall be by the shekel of the sanctuary' — what does the verse teach? Since it is stated 'you shall redeem,' might one [think it may be redeemed] with slaves, promissory notes, and land? The verse teaches: 'by the shekel of the sanctuary.' I have only selaim [coins]; from where [do we know] to include any movable item? The verse teaches: 'then it shall be redeemed according to your valuation.' If so, why is 'by the shekel' stated? To exclude slaves, promissory notes, and land." Rather, such is the manner of the Talmud, that it does not cite the primary source of the exposition, just as it is accustomed to cite (Ketubot 46b): "'In her youth, [in] her father's house' — all the earnings of her youth belong to her father," even though that [verse] is written regarding the annulment of vows; and similarly many [other instances].

Tosafot on Shabbat 128a:4:1.hebrew: רשב"ג אומר אף מטלטלין שברי זכוכית - משמע דמודה לת"ק דמתיר חרדל, והא דתנן "רשב"ג מתיר בלוף" — וכל שכן דמתיר בחרדל:
Tosafot on Shabbat 128a:4:1.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: One may even move glass shards - This implies that he agrees with the first Tanna, who permits [moving] mustard; and [similarly,] that which we learned in the Mishnah, "Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel permits [moving] arum" — all the more so does he permit [moving] mustard.
